title: Add tenant bootstrap FSM and values contract for safer airgap/on-prem installs
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Introduce a tenant bootstrap state-machine and an explicit values contract to make airgapped/on-prem installs deterministic and easier to validate. No behavioral breaking changes when not enabled; opt-in via values.bootstrap.enabled.
description:
Motivation: Private installs (airgap / on-prem) have accumulated multiple ad-hoc init jobs and templating overlays that are difficult to reason about during upgrades and rollbacks. This PR introduces a lightweight tenant bootstrap finite-state-machine (FSM) and an explicit 'bootstrap values contract' to: 1) sequence init steps deterministically, 2) expose safe knobs (timeouts, concurrency, backoff), and 3) provide a machine-readable values schema that CI and preflight checks can validate. This is opt-in: behavior is unchanged unless values.bootstrap.enabled = true.

What changed (high level):
- Add a bootstrap FSM implementation in templates/bootstrap-fsm.yaml that models phases: preflight -> image-prepull -> secret-sync -> db-migrate -> tenant-seed -> verify -> ready. Each phase maps to a Job with guarded transitions.
- Add values.bootstrap.* contract in values.schema.json and documented examples in values/bootstrap.example.yaml. Contract fields include: concurrencyLimit, phaseTimeouts, backoffStrategy, resumePolicy, maxRetries, and feature gates for airgap flows.
- New Helm helper templates (charts/_helpers.tpl) to render phase annotations and to inject rollback-fence annotations to prevent partial upgrades from leaving tenants in an inconsistent state.
- Add a lightweight preflight-check hook (templates/preflight-hook.yaml) wired to the FSM start phase to fail early on missing secrets/images in airgap mode.
- Add README section (charts/README-BOOTSTRAP.md) with recommended safe defaults for on-prem and an explanation of FSM states and failure modes.
- Conservative unit tests and a chart-testing workflow to validate the values contract and a small integration run in a KIND cluster for the happy-path.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc (linked in ENG-2217)
- [x] Helm lint and schema validations
- [x] Integration sanity run (KIND)
- [x] Docs and example values
- [x] Reviewed by infra/sre and charts teams

How to opt-in: set values.bootstrap.enabled = true and adjust values.bootstrap.phaseTimeouts and values.bootstrap.concurrencyLimit for your tenant scale. See charts/README-BOOTSTRAP.md for recommended profiles.

Notes on rollback safety: the FSM writes per-tenant bootstrap state to an init ConfigMap and attaches a rollback.fence annotation while a sequence is in-flight. The rollback guard prevents helm from performing a blind upgrade on resources that are mid-bootstrap unless the operator clears the fence or the resumePolicy allows automatic recovery. This avoids half-applied migrations and orphaned seed jobs.

Compatibility: The FSM is implemented using standard Kubernetes Job/ConfigMap primitives and follows existing RBAC scopes. No CRDs were introduced to keep the surface area minimal for airgapped customers.

References: ENG-2217 (design), tickets SUP-431 (customer-reported stuck-init) and INT-612 (upgrade flakiness during tenant seeding).

notes_for_backporters: No backport required. If backporting to a release branch used by on-prem customers, ensure the values.schema.json is added in the same commit to avoid upgrade validation failures.
examples_and_usage:
Example enable snippet:

bootstrap:
  enabled: true
  concurrencyLimit: 6
  phaseTimeouts:
    preflight: 5m
    imagePrepull: 15m
    migrate: 20m
    seed: 10m
    verify: 3m
  resumePolicy: auto
  backoffStrategy: exponential

See charts/bootstrap/values/bootstrap.example.yaml for full profiles (onprem.small/onprem.large/cloud-default).
